newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries mostly higher with no data slated.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries mostly higher with no data slated.

text.p: U.S. Treasury securities prices were mostly higher at Monday's opening as the market faced a session with virtually no data to trade upon.

The Group of Seven Industrialized Nations (G-7) met over the weekend in Denver, but nothing substantial or market moving for the bond market emerged, analysts said. However, the dollar appreciated sharply against the yen on a bland warning that the Japanese trade surplus needing to be contained.
The Treasury's 30-year bond was trading at 99-12/32, up 4/32, to yield 6.66 percent.

The crucial June nonfarm payrolls report was scheduled for next Friday, right after the the Federal Reserve's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meets on Wednesday and Thursday. Economists widely expected the FOMC to refrain from further tightening of monetary policy at next week's meeting.
The Fed last ratcheted up short-term interest rates by 25 basis points at its March 25 meeting.
Also due next week were data on personal income, new home sales, the National Association of Purchasing Managers survey, construction spending and factory orders.
At the short end of the maturity spectrum the three-month bill rate was up one basis point at 4.95 percent. Six-month and year bills were unchanged at 5.08 percent and 5.34 percent, respectively.
Two-year notes were down 1/32 at 100-14/32, yielding 6.00 percent. Five-year notes were up 2/32 at 100-28/32, yielding 6.29 percent. Ten-year notes were up 2/32 at 101-22/32, yielding 6.38 percent.
(( -- John P. Hughes, N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1663 ))
